  • Soulframe Builds & GuidesBest Soulframe Builds & Guides Database Welcome to our Soulframe Builds and Guides database. Here you can find a range of powerful builds for all classes in Soulframe, and guides that will help you learn to play Soulframe. Builds in Soulframe typically start by choosing your Pact (class), which defines which Arcanics (spells) and Arts (passives) you’ll have access to. Different pacts synergise with different equipment and suit different playstyles. Our build guides will explain all of these aspects, starting with the basics of the game and moving into more advanced details that will help you excel in Soulframe. Soulframe Builds You can find our full collection of Soulframe Builds below. All builds are updated after major Soulframe updates, so if they’re not already up to date with the latest game version, they will be very soon: Courage Builds Tethren Build Ode Tempest Melee Build Ode Tempest Lightning Mage Build Mora’s Hand Build Spirit Builds Oscelda Build Garren Rood Build Orengall Build Grace Builds Sirin Build Soulframe Beginner Guides Here are some guides that are especially useful for new Soulframe players: How to Unlock New Pacts “Find a Relic of Old ‘Fore the Ode” Explained Joineries & Reforging Guide Motes…

Best META Weapon Tier List – The First Descendant Season 4 E1

2026-09-01T13:50:01+00:00By Alcast|Categories: The First Descendant|
Listen to audio version of this article

Welcome to the META Weapon Tier List for The First Descendant. Here, I will show you my personal tier list of weapons. I have unlocked, maxed out, and played with all of the weapons in The First Descendant. Make sure to check out our The First Descendant Character Tier List, Onslaught Mode Tier List, and The First Descendant Builds Database (Weapons & Characters).

Updated for Season 4 Episode 1: This tier list has been fully revised to include the latest Season 4 Episode 1 balance changes.

The First Descendant Weapon Tier List Table of Contents:

  • Weapon Tier List Overview
  • S Tier: Meta Weapons – Must Have
  • A Tier: Powerful Weapons
  • B Tier: Good Weapons, but not a priority
  • C Tier: Low-Priority Weapons
  • D Tier: Backlog
  • Explained: What Makes Weapons Powerful
  • Terminology: Mobbing, Bossing, Stat-Stick, Debuffers

You can also view our The First Descendant Character Tier List if you wonder which characters you should prioritize.

TFD Wiki: We have expanded Alcasthq with tfd.gameslantern.com, a Wiki & Database for anything related to The First Descendant. Use the Character Editor or the Weapon Editor to theorycraft and create builds yourself. Browse Descendants, Weapons, Leaderboard Loadouts or use the Compare Tool. There are plenty of other features you can check out, too!

The First Descendant Best Weapon Tier List

You can also view our Ultimate Weapon List for The First Descendant if you want to learn more about each weapon. Generally, it is recommended to stick to S or A Tier weapons if you are new to the game and you don’t have unlimited resources to max out all weapons. Of course, if you have all META weapons, you can pick whatever you want next! Some weapons are fun to use but might not be that strong.

For each weapon, I will also specify whether it is ranked for Single-Target or Area of Effect damage. Generally, most weapons are only used for one thing, but some also can be useful for both mobbing and bossing.

  1. It is important to note, that you must have maximum level godroll weapon cores on your weapons for them to unleash their true potential. Especially, Fire Rate godrolls are essential.
  2. Below the Tier List, you will find an explanation of each weapon for what it’s being used for.

S-Tier – Must-Have Meta Weapons

Here are all the  S-Tier Weapons in our The First Descendant Weapon Tier List. These weapons are generally a must-have in the current meta.

Important: It is crucial to remember that these rankings here are only accurate if you have maxed out weapons, especially max level godroll weapon core stats are important. For example, missing out on 2% Fire Rate Core stats on Restored Relic halves its actual fire rate.

Stat Stick Transcendent Weapons that boost attribute damage tremendously:

  • ATR-0 Prototype (Non-Attribute)
  • Volcanic Heart (Fire)
  • Frost Blossom (Chill)
  • Nightmare Launcher (Toxic)
  • Sparky (Electric)

Armis works great on weapon-based Descendants.

Unleashed Instinct is great for characters like Raven or Gley.

Thunder Cage is easy to get and deals massive AoE damage. You will be able to easily clear any content with this weapon.

Hammer & Anvil has crazy high AoE damage in its secondary mode. Make sure to shoot above the enemies so the bullets drop down and explode in a wide area.

Albion Cavalry Gun and the Restored Relic are a great combo to own for single-target & AoE damage.

Next, we have the Malevolent weapon, which is a beast for any mobbing situation. The weapon spreads its blades among many targets, dealing massive AoE damage. Malevolent also has a strong weapon core setup, making it even better!

The Last Dagger is a powerful single-target focused weapon that can deal massive burst damage with the correct module spec. It is definitely worth maxing it out.

Whirlwind is a powerful AoE chill-focused weapon.

Eye of the Typhoon is a powerful AoE weapon primarely used by the character Serena due to how her ultimate works with weapons.

Shadow is also great for mobbing, its special ability deals massive AoE damage and also deals good damage against bosses.

Hypernova is a great mobbing weapon that can be thrown and then pulls all enemies into its center for easy kills.

Ancient Knight is a strong assault rifle specifically made for Serena to destroy colossus. However, I find the Albion Cavalry Gun to be an overall better weapon. Therefore only use Ancient Knight if you have already maxed out most other weapons in this bracket.

Secret Garden is a powerful “Stat Stick” often used on characters like Freyna, Ines, Lepic, and Nell. This weapon buffs tech damage tremendously. On top of that, it also has nice cores that increase your sprint speed and or grapple hook recharge time. You don’t actually shoot this gun; it is just here to enhance the skill power of your Descendant and increase mobility, hence “Stat Stick”.

Peace Maker is another stat stick that has no other value than to increase your sprint speed and or grapple hook recharge time. Peace Maker also has the highest base movement speed of any weapon, therefore increasing your mobility even further.

A-TAMS is the strongest sniper rifle in The First Desendant. It is often used with Luna (with Battlefield Concert mod), Hailey, Serena, and Sharen.

A-Tier – Powerful Weapons

A-Tier weapons are generally good weapons but are outclassed by the S-Tier cohort. I would prioritize Greg’s Reversed Fate and Blue Beetle first in this section.

B-Tier – Good Weapons

These weapons are good but I would only craft these if I have already finished all S and A-Tier weapons. Voltia is very useful in the Void Vessel because it nullifies the shields that monsters run around with. However, you coul also simply slot the Veil Analyzer Module on any weapon to have the same effect.

C-Tier – Low-Priority Weapons

These weapons are not worth crafting. Wave of Light can be useful to regen MP instantly, but often not needed.

D-Tier – Backlog Weapons

Useless weapons.

What Makes A Weapon Powerful In The First Descendant?

Weapons have different mechanics in terms of how much power they can achieve. Now in this section of the tier list I want to showcase you an example of how much extra power you can actually gain.

  • Modules: Most flexible mechanic, you can swap out modules any time without having to pay anything.
  • Readjustments: Enhance the power with further stats.
  • Cores: Enhance the power tremendously with max level cores.

Let’s take a look at one of the best examples: Restored Relic.

The First Descendant Terminology

Weapons have different use cases in The First Descendant. Here is a quick explanation of the terminology often used in combination with weapons.

Mobbing

Mobbing weapons are used for any content that requires massive area of effect damage. So anything that can deal with massive hordes of monsters at once.

Bossing

Bossing weapons specialize in killing Colossus bosses, they are often built solely for single-target. Sometimes they are also built to defeat bosses at the end of a dungeon.

Stat Stick

A Stat Stick weapon is simply being held to give characters additional buffs. For example the Secret Garden buffs tech skill damage tremendously, but also buffs your movement speed and grapple hook recharge, increasing your overall mobility.

Debuffer

Debuff weapons are used to reduce the enemies effectiveness. For example the Clairvoyance beam rifle reduces the chill resistance of enemies. Allowing you or your teammates to deal more damage with chill-based attribute weapons.
